svg.title: Unpacking a message
svg.text: Stage 5, Unpack + Report: 77 bits become "CQ UY5AX KO70"
r1 = "/R" suffix flag, R1 = "R" before the grid or report. Both are 0 here. A call is 6 characters from a fixed alphabet, packed into 28 bits; the
lowest values are reserved for tokens such as DE, QRZ, CQ, "CQ DX" and "CQ 123". The grid field also carries reports (−12, R+05) and RRR, RR73, 73.
Other message types the stage understands
The two examples in the first row are real decodes from my tests; the others are made-up illustrations of each format.
Long or unusual calls (DA0FONTANE, KH1/KH7Z) don't fit in 28 bits, so the other station appears as a short hash: 10, 12 or 22 bits.
Stage 5 remembers every call it has decoded in full, with its hashes. Until it has heard a call once, the hash prints as <...>.
In my test run, the slot at :30 printed "<JR5MJS> DA0FONTANE" because JR5MJS had been decoded in full one slot earlier.
Then the stage measures dB (signal against the noise floor nearby, scaled to WSJT-X's 2500 Hz), DT (start time − 0.5 s) and the audio frequency.
